title: Belief framing is a fixed template: absurd and self-contradictory claims get the same 'GPT-5.6' hypotheses, with insufficientEvidence=false
reproducibility: Always (3/3 independent sessions with semantically unrelated claims)
journey: Start sample → enter any claim → 'Compare two explanations'
environment: Cloudflare Worker; sample mode; Chrome browser; 2026-07-19 UTC
steps: Open / and click 'Try verified sample'.
Enter claim A: 'Purple bananas taste better on Tuesdays, therefore this notebook's score is meaningless.' → Compare two explanations.
Repeat in a fresh sample with claim B: a self-contradictory claim asserting both generalization and its negation.
Compare framed hypotheses across sessions and against swarm bundle agent5_proof_record.json (sensible churn claim).
Fetch /api/sessions/<id> and inspect beliefTest.
expected: Framing sensitive to the claim; off-topic/nonsense claims refused or flagged ('unsupported evidence is refused, not guessed'); contradictory claims detected.
actual: currentHypothesis/competingHypothesis/evidenceRefs/alternatives/decisiveIntervention/uncertainty are BYTE-IDENTICAL across all three claims; only learnerClaim echoes input verbatim; uncertainty.confidence=0.93 and insufficientEvidence=false even for nonsense; the contradiction is never detected and the system arbitrarily keeps the 'generalizes' framing. belief_test.proposed event actor is 'system' with modelId 'leakage-customer-churn-belief-v1' (a prompt-template slug); there is no model/gpt actor in the event chain; proposed event outputHash differs per claim, so the hash binds the claim but the content is constant.

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: 3 sessions: agent5 (sensible), session_297ad7b7 (absurd), session_aadb0d7d (contradictory) → identical framing text

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: beliefTest.uncertainty {confidence:0.93, insufficientEvidence:false} for the purple-bananas claim

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: screenshots of step-2 framing for absurd and contradictory claims

likely_cause: Sample mode uses a stored Belief Spec template (modelId=leakage-customer-churn-belief-v1); no model is invoked in sample mode (judge page: 'no account or model credential'), and no input validation/refusal layer exists for claim text.
unverified: Whether live /new mode actually calls GPT-5.6 and behaves input-sensitively (file input untestable).
learner_impact: Any words a learner writes are 'understood' as the same leakage misconception; the product pretends to have read and framed the learner's idea when it has not.
judge_impact: The headline claim 'GPT-5.6 frames beliefs' is not demonstrated in the only two inspectable paths; judges testing with creative claims get canned output.
trust_impact: Core epistemic promise ('reality answers, not prose') is violated at the framing layer: prose is templated and never refuses.
recommended_correction: Label sample framing as a pre-authored example ('In this sample, the belief spec is pre-written; live mode frames your claim'), and/or invoke the real model in sample mode; add claim-level sufficiency checks that set insufficientEvidence=true and refuse off-topic input.
smallest_correction: Add an in-flow disclosure line on step 2: 'These two explanations are pre-authored for the bundled sample, not generated from your claim.'
acceptance_criteria: Two different claims produce visibly different framings OR the UI explicitly labels the framing as pre-authored; nonsense claims trigger a visible insufficient-evidence state.
regression_test: Submit 3 semantically distinct claims; assert framings differ or disclosure banner present; assert nonsense claim yields insufficientEvidence=true or refusal.
dependencies: None for disclosure; model-backed framing depends on live pipeline.
score_leverage: High — directly undermines the Technological Implementation narrative if unaddressed.

title: 'Runtime Codex' has no runtime role in any reachable path: codex events are empty markers; compile→verify takes 360ms from a 5-day-old stored artifact
reproducibility: Always (sample path; replay is the same stored evidence by design)
journey: Sample lesson through Test and Repair
prerequisites: Complete prediction lock in a sample session
steps: Complete a sample session; fetch /api/sessions/<id>/events.
Inspect codex-actor events (lab.compilation_started, patch.compilation_started).
Compare timestamps with the following verifier events; inspect lab.verified payload.
expected: Codex compiles a bounded plan at runtime, emitting artifacts (plan, adapter, tests) attributable to the session; verification follows compilation.
actual: codex events carry payload:{} and empty outputHashes — no plan, adapter, tests, or diff anywhere in the event stream. lab.verified fires 360ms after compilation_started with source 'stored-approved-leakage-v1', recordedAt 2026-07-14T11:18:03Z (5 days before the session), image counterlab-runner:local. patch.verified fires 1.17s after patch.compilation_started; patchHash 18712546… and diff bytes are identical across independent sessions and to the replay's stored patch. No *.compilation_completed event exists.

evidence.label: Observed in network response
evidence.detail: events seq 5/6 and 13/14 with timestamps and payloads

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: generatedAdapter.sha256 ed70072a…, commitHash 1050fa76…, publicTestsReportHash 30663c3b…, patchHash 18712546… identical in agent5's independent bundle

likely_cause: Sample/replay modes serve the stored-approved fixture from 2026-07-14 and emit marker events to simulate the live pipeline; live Codex is only wired to the untestable /new path.
unverified: Whether /new live mode performs real Codex compilation (health endpoint claims liveCodex: configured).
learner_impact: Streamed 'compiling/verifying' progress is theatre; learners watching 'Codex at work' see a replay.
judge_impact: Criterion 1 asks 'how thoroughly and skillfully does the project use Codex' — in every judge-reachable path the answer is: it doesn't run; the only genuine Codex/verifier trace (compilerTrace in the replay API) shows two REJECTED runs and a later regeneration, and is never shown in the UI.
trust_impact: The four-authority architecture diagram ('Runtime Codex compiles the test plan… No blurred hand-offs') is not operative in demo paths.
recommended_correction: Either wire sample mode to the real pipeline (cheap fixture-backed kernel but genuinely compiled plan), or label the sample as 'recorded pipeline evidence' at the Test/Repair steps, and surface the compilerTrace (including rejections) in the replay UI.
smallest_correction: Change step-3 copy from 'CounterLab verified the plan' to 'This plan was verified once on 2026-07-14; the sample replays that evidence' and link the compilerTrace.
acceptance_criteria: codex events contain compiled artifact hashes produced after session start, or UI/API clearly marks the compilation as recorded replay.
regression_test: Create session; assert (lab.verified.timestamp - lab.compilation_started.timestamp) is consistent with real compilation OR lab.verified.payload.recordedAt is disclosed in UI.
dependencies: None for labelling; real compilation needs live worker pipeline.
score_leverage: High — the Codex-usage criterion is the published tiebreaker.

title: Sample lesson presents stored 2026-07-14 evidence as session verification; labelling asymmetry vs replay path
journey: Sample lesson Test step and Proof page
prerequisites: Run a sample session to step 3
steps: Compare replay banner copy with sample-flow copy at equivalent steps.
Read the 'Verification progress' and 'Evidence & proof' panels in sample mode.
expected: Equivalent honesty: sample should say as clearly as replay that evidence is recorded/stored and not computed for this session.
actual: Replay says 'This path reconstructs recorded events and computed payloads. It is not a live model run.' Sample says 'Instant sample'/'Verified sample', 'CounterLab verified the plan', 'Test plan verified'; the word 'recorded' appears once in small print ('passed its recorded verification'). The Proof Capsule bundles the stored verification (recordedAt 2026-07-14, source stored-approved-leakage-v1) without marking it stored inside the bundle.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: replay banner vs sample step-3 copy

likely_cause: Intentional differentiation of 'sample' vs 'replay' labelling; sample treated as sufficient disclosure.
learner_impact: Learners plausibly believe a computation/verification just ran for them.
judge_impact: Judge page claims sample is 'always labelled as a sample' — technically true, but the stronger 'verified now' framing persists in-flow.
trust_impact: Medium-high; the product's core value is epistemic hygiene, so half-labelled provenance cuts deep.
recommended_correction: Apply replay-grade disclosure to sample mode: persistent 'Recorded evidence — replayed for this session' note at Test/Repair/Proof.
smallest_correction: One-line provenance note under 'Test plan verified'.
acceptance_criteria: A first-time user can state, unprompted, that no computation ran for their session.
regression_test: Copy audit of steps 3/6/proof for the words 'recorded'/'replayed'.

title: Same verified result carries two different 'resultHash' values across paths (a6ae7652… vs 25016542…); fingerprints differ too
journey: Compare sample proof and replay evidence
steps: Note result hash shown in sample result table and in bundle verifiedResultSet.resultHash.
Compare with lab.verified payload resultHash and replay API result.resultHash.
Compare featureSetFingerprint per run across the two payloads.
expected: One canonical hash for one canonical result payload; the displayed hash matches the verifiable artifact regardless of path.
actual: Sample UI and verifiedResultSet show a6ae7652e04e…; lab.verified payload and replay (API + UI) show 2501654264b9…. Within ONE proof bundle the two resultHash fields disagree. featureSetFingerprint random_row_split: 1fd4ea95… (sample) vs 621d1d17… (replay); identity_ablation: 9641773f… vs 25611036b…. Metrics identical to 12 decimal places, so the numbers are the same fixture; the hash domains differ. 'canonical_result_hash' is a verified invariant, yet the canonical value is path-dependent.

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: hash comparisons across my bundle, agent5 bundle, replay API

likely_cause: Two serialization/canonicalization versions of the result set (replay payload lacks pipelineFingerprint; different feature-set fingerprint inputs), or the verifier-approved hash commits to a different payload than the kernel-emitted one.
unverified: Which hash (if either) is reproducible via ./scripts/reproduce-session.sh (no shell internet).
learner_impact: Low direct, but a curious learner comparing sample and replay sees contradictory 'fingerprints'.
judge_impact: A judge verifying hash-chain claims finds the displayed result hash is not stable across the product's own paths.
trust_impact: Hash-chaining is the product's integrity story; ambiguity here is material.
recommended_correction: Publish the canonicalization (hash domain separation labels, e.g., 'kernel-result-hash' vs 'verifier-approved-hash'), or unify to one canonical hash and explain any intentional difference in the bundle.
smallest_correction: Rename fields to distinct names (kernelResultHash vs verifierApprovedResultHash) and document both in the proof bundle.
acceptance_criteria: A third party can recompute or at least explain every displayed hash from the bundled payload.
regression_test: Cross-path hash equality test for identical fixture results, or explicit schema fields distinguishing the two.

title: Nonsense claim is carried into a signed 'verified' Proof Capsule (Reasoning Diff 'Before' = 'Purple bananas…')
journey: Complete sample with an off-topic claim
user: learner, judge, anyone verifying the capsule
prerequisites: Complete all 6 steps with any claim text
steps: Enter an absurd claim; complete the loop; open the proof page and bundle.
Inspect reasoningDiff.dimensions.belief.before and beliefTest.learnerClaim.
expected: The proof attests to a coherent learning episode; input that cannot support the framed belief test is refused before verification.
actual: The HMAC-signed proof bundle binds: learnerClaim='Purple bananas taste better on Tuesdays…', the canned leakage framing, insufficientEvidence=false, confidence 0.93, a VERIFIED experiment, and a Reasoning Diff whose 'Before' is the nonsense sentence. The capsule is cryptographically consistent and semantically meaningless.
likely_cause: No semantic gate between claim intake and proof issuance; proof integrity covers tamper-evidence only, not meaningfulness.
learner_impact: A learner can generate an authoritative-looking certificate for gibberish; the certificate's epistemic meaning collapses.
judge_impact: Judges can reproduce a 'verified proof' for a nonsense claim in ~3 minutes.
trust_impact: High — the product's output artifact does not mean what it appears to mean.
recommended_correction: Gate proof issuance on a meaningful claim-binding check; at minimum surface claim/framing mismatch warnings in the capsule.
smallest_correction: Add a visible 'claim was not analyzed' flag in the capsule when running in template mode.
acceptance_criteria: Nonsense claims cannot yield a VERIFIED capsule without explicit warning.
regression_test: E2E: nonsense claim → assert refusal or conspicuous warning in bundle.

title: 'Not enough evidence' bricks the session: internal state-machine error leaks to UI, no recovery path
route: /session/<id> step 2 → 'More ways to respond' → 'Not enough evidence'
prerequisites: Reach step 2 in a sample session
steps: Click 'Not enough evidence'.
Observe return to step 1 with claim text intact and 'Compare two explanations' still offered.
Click 'Compare two explanations' again.
expected: Either a terminal 'insufficient evidence' outcome screen with a restart CTA, or a genuine editable retry.
actual: Session state becomes terminal INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (API: state=INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, version=3) while the UI renders the editable Question step; clicking 'Compare two explanations' shows raw internal error 'Invalid transition from INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE to BELIEF_TEST_PROPOSED'. The page then switches to 'RESULT WITHHELD — No verified result was released. CounterLab will not substitute bundled sample evidence for this session. Return to the test and try again.' — but there is no working path to try again (stepper shows Question; no functional form). The fail-closed withholding is commendable; the dead-end UX and leaked internals are not. Also: belief_test.insufficient_evidence event has inputHashes:[] — it does not bind to the belief test it rejects.
likely_cause: UI does not treat INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE as terminal; state machine rejects the transition; no recovery route.
unverified: Whether 'Reject' behaves identically (same class of bug, not separately exercised).
learner_impact: A learner who honestly says 'not enough evidence' is punished with a broken session and a cryptic error.
judge_impact: Judges exploring the refusal affordance hit an internal error within 2 clicks.
trust_impact: Medium — the one honest refusal path is the buggiest path in the product.
recommended_correction: Render a proper terminal 'Insufficient evidence' outcome screen with a 'Start a new session' CTA; never leak transition tables to users.
smallest_correction: Catch the transition error and route to the withheld screen immediately with a working restart button.
acceptance_criteria: Choosing 'Not enough evidence' leads to a stable terminal screen with recovery CTA; no internal error strings displayed.
regression_test: E2E refusal-path test asserting terminal screen + working restart.

title: Genuine reject-reject-regenerate compilerTrace (incl. generationIsolation PARTIAL) is API-only; UI and judge copy show a success-only story
steps: Fetch /api/replays/leakage-01 and read compilerTrace.trace and isolation blocks.
Walk the replay UI end-to-end looking for the rejected runs.
expected: The advertised 'genuine reject–repair trace' shows the rejections and the disclosed isolation limitation.
actual: compilerTrace records: generate COMPLETED → external_verifier REJECTED (candidate_execution) → repair_1 REJECTED → repair_2 REJECTED ('No result was authorized') → later_generate COMPLETED ('not presented as repair attempt 3') → VERIFIED. generationIsolation: PARTIAL ('host App Server process read global skill files… not proven'). None of this appears anywhere in the replay UI, the proof page, or judge copy; the replay UI shows only the final VERIFIED story. The repair loop never actually succeeded in the recorded evidence — verification passed on a fresh later generation, so 'reject–repair trace' overstates it.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: replay UI end state shows only verified patch and reproduction commands

likely_cause: UI scope cut: the honest trace exists in data but was never surfaced.
learner_impact: Learners miss the most instructive part: verification can and does reject.
judge_impact: Judges who find the API trace see strong evidence; judges who don't, see marketing. The discrepancy is discoverable.
trust_impact: Medium — the data is honest, the presentation is selective.
recommended_correction: Add a 'verification history' panel to the replay showing all six trace stages, counterexamples, and the PARTIAL isolation caveat.
smallest_correction: Link 'View the full compiler trace (JSON)' from the replay proof panel.
acceptance_criteria: Rejected stages and isolation limitation visible in UI.
regression_test: UI test asserting the rejected stages render for replay leakage-01.
score_leverage: Medium (converts a hidden asset into visible trust)

title: Event-chain attribution gaps: no model/gpt actor, learner claim has no event, refusal event unbound
steps: Fetch events for a completed and a refused session.
Check actors, modelId fields, input/output hash bindings.
expected: Every material action attributable: claim submission (learner), framing (model actor with real model id), refusal bound to the rejected artifact.
actual: belief_test.proposed is actor 'system' with modelId 'leakage-customer-churn-belief-v1' (a template/prompt slug; versions.model in the bundle is the same slug, not a model version). No event records the learner's claim submission. belief_test.insufficient_evidence has inputHashes:[] — it does not reference the belief test it rejects. codex events are empty (see A10-02).
likely_cause: Event schema designed for the happy path; provenance fields reused for template mode.
unverified: Whether live mode emits a gpt actor with a real model id.
learner_impact: Indirect — the audit trail understates what happened to the learner's own words.
judge_impact: The 'actor-attributed hash-chained events' claim is only partially true; attribution is weakest exactly where AI involvement is claimed.
recommended_correction: Add claim.submitted (learner) and belief framing events with honest actor/model fields (e.g., actor 'template' in sample mode); bind refusal events via inputHashes.
smallest_correction: Rename modelId to templateId in sample-mode events and bundles.
acceptance_criteria: Every UI-visible step maps to ≥1 event with truthful actor attribution.
regression_test: Schema test: refusal events must have non-empty inputHashes referencing the rejected belief test.

title: Home claim box discards text into a dead live gate; live intake stalls forever with no refusal, error, or guidance
steps: Type a class-imbalance question in the home claim box; submit.
Land on /new 'Live generation'; click 'Continue with my notebook' without a file.
Type an off-topic claim ('Why is the sky blue?') and wait.
expected: Claim text carried into the session; without a notebook, a clear message that evidence is required; off-topic text refused per 'Unsupported evidence is refused, not guessed.'
actual: Claim text vanishes; /new shows a notebook gate; continuing without upload leaves artifact 'Preparing artifact… / Pending intake / Support decision Pending' indefinitely — no timeout, no error, no refusal, no CTA; 'Compare two explanations' never enables; 0 events; no session created. The advertised refusal behavior has no reachable UX for text input.

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: home claim → /new gate with text lost

likely_cause: Claim box is a navigation affordance, not an intake; live pipeline requires a notebook artifact before any processing; no client-side validation messaging.
unverified: Behavior with an actual notebook file (file input untestable).
learner_impact: The primary CTA ('Ask like chat') silently swallows the learner's question and strands them.
judge_impact: A judge's first typed interaction is a dead end.
trust_impact: Medium — the refusal promise is untestable in the only text-entry path.
recommended_correction: Persist claim text into the session draft; add explicit 'notebook required to continue' and 'claim unsupported — here's why' states with copy.
smallest_correction: Carry the claim into the /new textarea and show a 'Waiting for notebook evidence' notice instead of 'Preparing artifact…'.
acceptance_criteria: Text claims are never silently discarded; pending states resolve to a message within N seconds.
regression_test: E2E: submit claim without notebook → assert claim preserved + visible guidance.

title: Template hypothesis is presented as the learner's own explanation ('Your current explanation… Does this capture your view?')
steps: Enter any claim; reach 'Two explanations, one fair test'.
Read attribution copy.
expected: Clear authorship: 'CounterLab's example reading of this evidence' vs 'your words'.
actual: The canned statement 'The notebook's random-row test accuracy demonstrates generalization to new customers.' is headlined 'Your current explanation' and the learner is asked to confirm 'this captures my view' — even when their claim said the opposite (or nonsense). Authorship of model/template prose is blurred into the learner's identity.
likely_cause: Pedagogical framing choice ('make the learner own a hypothesis') colliding with template content.
learner_impact: Learners may adopt a belief they never held; the 'reasoning diff' later measures change against a baseline the learner never wrote.
trust_impact: Medium — attribution honesty is core to this product's thesis.
recommended_correction: Label authorship: 'CounterLab's reading of this evidence (pre-authored for the sample)'; require the learner to pick or write their own statement before the label 'your explanation' is used.
smallest_correction: Change headline to 'A possible reading of this evidence'.
acceptance_criteria: No system-authored sentence is labeled as the learner's without an explicit adoption action.
regression_test: Copy audit test for 'Your current explanation'.

title: Transfer gate glyphs read as inverted for the selection task (leaky feature marked × when correctly selected)
steps: Select 'Centered rolling target' as the feature that crosses NOW (the correct answer to the question asked).
Observe the glyph.
expected: Selection feedback should distinguish 'your choice is correct' from 'this feature is dangerous'.
actual: Selecting the leaky feature (the correct answer to 'Which feature crosses NOW?') renders 'reads later outcomes ×' beside it; the safe feature shows 'uses available information ✓'. The ✓/× marks feature safety, not answer correctness, but in a quiz context it reads as 'you picked wrong' — consistent with the swarm's 'transfer gate glyphs inverted' observation.
likely_cause: One icon set overloaded for two meanings (feature risk vs answer correctness).
learner_impact: Confusing mixed signals at the exact moment of assessment.
recommended_correction: Separate indicators: keep risk annotations neutral ('reads future data') and add explicit correct/incorrect feedback after 'Check transfer'.
smallest_correction: Replace ✓/× with neutral tags ('safe at prediction time' / 'reads future').
acceptance_criteria: Usability test: learners correctly interpret feedback on first attempt.
regression_test: Snapshot test of transfer feedback states.

title: Verifier depth is hash-only for users: 18-invariant/12-mutation report bodies are never exposed; replay step-3 prose says 'has now run' in stored mode
steps: Look for per-invariant evidence behind externalVerifierReportHash 9304e077… / reportHash 0926dcec….
Read replay step-3 copy.
expected: Inspectable invariant/mutation evidence (or a documented reason it is withheld); stored-mode copy in past tense.
actual: Only report hashes are exposed; no endpoint returns the verifier report body (404s on unknown routes suggest no hidden route; not exhaustively mapped). Replay step 3 says 'CounterLab has now run and checked the fairer test' — present-tense, conflicting with its own replay banner. Sample bundle limitations do disclose 'Docker enforcement is evidence for this local run, not a formal sandbox proof' (good), but only inside the JSON.
likely_cause: Report content considered internal; copy reuse between live and replay templates.
unverified: Whether a report endpoint exists outside the documented API surface.
judge_impact: Medium-low — judges cannot independently check what the 18 invariants asserted.
recommended_correction: Publish the invariant/mutation report bodies alongside hashes (or in the proof download); fix replay tense.
smallest_correction: Include the 18+12 checklist with per-item evidence strings in the proof bundle JSON.
regression_test: API test fetching report by hash.

title: Session footer 'Evidence & proof' counter shows '0 events' while the events API returns multiple events
steps: Observe footer 'N events' counter.
Compare with /api/sessions/<id>/events length.
actual: Footer showed '0 events' on a session with 3 recorded events (incl. session.created and belief_test.insufficient_evidence).
likely_cause: Counter fed by a different (client-side) event list that fails to load or filters kinds.
learner_impact: Undermines the transparency affordance ('Open' the event log).
recommended_correction: Bind counter to the canonical events endpoint.
regression_test: UI test comparing counter to API length.

title: Always-positive funnel: any claim + brute-forceable 2×2 transfer gate (unlimited retries) always yields a VERIFIED patch and signed capsule
steps: Enter arbitrary text; confirm framing; lock any prediction; reveal result; build rule; answer transfer gate.
Deliberately answer wrong: observe 'Transfer not yet passed' with unlimited immediate retries.
Answer correctly: reach VERIFIED patch + proof.
expected: A system whose thesis is 'reality can say no' should have meaningful failure surfaces on the main path.
actual: The only gates are: confirm pre-written framing (one click), lock a prediction (no wrong answer — even 'I am unsure' proceeds), and a 2×2 multiple-choice transfer with instant feedback and unlimited retries. Every persistent user reaches 'VERIFIED patch + signed Proof Capsule'. The sole negative terminal state requires voluntarily choosing 'Not enough evidence'/'Reject' — which bricks the session (A10-06). Wrong predictions are falsified by the result (good), but the flow proceeds identically regardless.

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: failed transfer then passed; nonsense claim to full verified proof

likely_cause: Pedagogical design optimized for completion; failure states treated as edge cases.
unverified: Whether live mode has stricter gates.
learner_impact: Completion is guaranteed; 'verification' of the learner's transfer is not discriminating.
judge_impact: Medium — the product's rigor story is thinner than its verification story.
recommended_correction: Make at least one gate discriminating (e.g., limited transfer attempts with a meaningful 'not yet' state that teaches, or a claim-sufficiency check on entry).
smallest_correction: Cap transfer retries and add a reflective 'why was this wrong' step before retry.
acceptance_criteria: A disengaged user cannot reach a verified capsule by clicking through.
regression_test: E2E brute-force test asserting a stopping condition exists.
